item.title: Sturgill Simpson is releasing a new Johnny Blue Skies album in March, but you won’t be able to stream it
item.description: Simpson and his band the Dark Clouds plan to share their “pure, unfiltered, unapologetic, relentless disco-hedonism” on Mutiny After Midnight, which arrives March 13 on vinyl, CD, and cassette only.

item.title: 13 new albums to stream this week
item.description: The new albums from Jill Scott, Nashpaints, and August Ponthier should be at the top of your queue today. Tap in and find a new obsession.

item.title: Lorne Michaels is getting the documentary treatment from Roadrunner's Morgan Neville
item.description: The film, out in April, purports to offer "unprecedented access to the quiet force who shaped American comedy."

item.title: The Lemonheads’ Evan Dando accused of sending unsolicited sexually explicit videos
item.description: Dando has been hospitalized for “comprehensive help from experienced doctors and mental health professionals” this week, according to one of his representatives.

item.title: Take a dip with a first-look at Jane Schoenbrun's Teenage Sex And Death At Camp Miasma
item.description: Hannah Einbinder and Gillian Anderson star in Schoenbrun's follow-up to I Saw The TV Glow, coming out this August.

item.title: Sounds like Doug Liman and Pete Davidson's Bitcoin biopic is being filmed in a hellish AI void
item.description: Pete Davidson and Casey Affleck are set to star in Killing Satoshi, while the role of "backgrounds and scenery" will be played by AI slop.

item.title: Uneasy Hollywood suddenly realizes it hasn't rebooted Charlie's Angels in a minute
item.description: Seven years after the last Charlie's Angels movie bombed in theaters, Sony is reportedly trying again.
